subject: SCIM + SSO provisioning consolidation RFI — IdWorks integration
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@idworks.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: idsys-procurement@idworks.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SCIM/SSO provisioning consolidation RFI — integration details needed

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for agreeing to take a look — IdWorks is consolidating three legacy provisioning paths into a single SCIM-driven flow and we have a few detailed questions for vendors as part of the RFI. Attached is a short spreadsheet with the enumerated requirements (scim_requirements.xlsx). High-level asks:

- Do you support full SCIM PATCH (add/replace/remove) and bulk PATCH operations?
- Can SCIM be scoped per-tenant (multi-tenant single instance) with attribute namespaces and transformations?
- How do you handle soft-deletes vs hard-deletes for user objects and group membership reconciliation?
- For SSO: do you support both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated SAML flows, and OIDC as an alternative? Any recommended best practice?
- Describe admin role delegation (granular RBAC) and whether delegated admins can provision users via SCIM or only via Console/API.

We need implementation details and evidence (logs, example mappings) to include with the procurement packet. Can you also indicate typical rollout options (canary/batch sync) and expected downtime for initial syncs on a 200k-user tenant?

Appreciate any technical artifacts you can share.

Best,
Alice
Director, Identity & Access
IdWorks

Attachments: scim_requirements.xlsx (Spreadsheet, 22KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@idworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SCIM/SSO provisioning consolidation RFI — integration details needed

Hi Alice,

Thanks for the detailed RFI — I've gone through the spreadsheet and provided concise answers below. I've attached a short package (redwood_scim_admin_controls.pdf) with sample mappings, admin role matrix, and a high-level rollout plan. If helpful, we can follow up with a workshop to walk through mappings and run a test sync.

Summary answers (short):
- SCIM operations: Full support for SCIM v2 including PATCH (add/replace/remove) and incremental bulk operations. We also support transactional bulk endpoints for large initial loads to reduce reconciliation windows.
- Multi-tenant scoping & transformations: Yes. Our SCIM service supports tenant-scoped attribute namespaces and a transformation layer that can perform attribute renaming, concatenation, and conditional mapping (examples in the attached PDF).
- Soft-delete behavior: By default we implement "soft-delete" via an external deletion marker (active=false) and a configurable retention window before hard-delete. Admins can override behavior per-tenant. Reconciliation engine supports tombstone reconciliation to avoid re-creating deleted accounts on subsequent syncs.
- SSO: We support both SAML (IdP/SP initiated) and OIDC. For your use case we typically recommend SAML for mature enterprise IdPs and OIDC for modern cloud-native apps. We provide attribute/claim mapping templates for both.
- RBAC & delegated admins: Granular RBAC is supported. Delegated admins can be granted scoped provisioning rights (e.g., can manage users in subset of tenants or only specific groups). Provisioning via SCIM can be permitted to delegated roles through scoped client credentials (OAuth2 client per admin segment) or via API tokens tied to a role.
- Rollout recommendations: Canary by tenant (10% of users), followed by batched incremental syncs (daily delta) and a final bulk reconcile. For a 200k-user tenant initial bulk import with optimized transactional bulk should finish within low-hours (3–6 hours) depending on provisioning rate and attribute volume; full reconcile depends on group membership churn.

Next steps:
1) We'll schedule a 90-minute technical workshop with our integration engineering team to walk through your spreadsheet and sample mappings.
2) Provide a short test dataset and read-only SCIM account for a pilot.
3) Share a suggested rollout calendar and runbook.

I've attached the detailed PDF and a small mapping example file; Ben will follow up with the technical playbook and Pernod (our Integration PM) will coordinate dates.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_scim_admin_controls.pdf (PDF, 180KB)

Kimberly —

Thanks, this is helpful. A few follow-ups after reviewing the PDF:

- Can you confirm support for SCIM PATCH that includes nested complex attributes (e.g., multiple emails with types and primary flags) and how primary selection is handled on conflict?
- For attribute transformations: do you allow regex transforms and conditional mapping (e.g., map employeeType -> group if department matches 'Engineering')?
- On the RBAC side: can delegated admins trigger bulk reconcilations or is that restricted to org-admins? We need auditors to be able to see who performed reconciliation and have read-only access to logs.

Also, do you provide example audit log exports (CSV/JSON) for provisioning events with token-level attribution? Please include retention defaults in your response.

Regards,
Alice

(On the procurement side, we may need a short proof-of-concept with 5k test users prior to awarding the integration contract.)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@idworks.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 07:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SCIM/SSO provisioning consolidation RFI — integration details needed

Hi Alice,

Following up with the more technical side of things — answering your specific questions:

- Nested complex attributes: Yes. Our SCIM implementation handles complex arrays (e.g., emails[type, value, primary]) and supports atomic decisions on primary selection. The reconciliation engine will honor a primary=true flag if present; otherwise we apply a deterministic selection rule (newest verified email wins) which can be overridden via mapping rules.
- Regex & conditional transforms: We support a transformation DSL that includes regex capture/replace, conditional mappings, and computed fields (concat, substring, lookup). You can write a rule like: if department == 'Engineering' then addMember('eng-all') or map employeeType -> group with a lookup table.
- Delegated admins & bulk reconcile: Delegated admins can be granted the ability to trigger bulk/transactional reconciles but that is an explicit permission in the RBAC policy (we don't enable it by default). All actions are audited; token-level attribution is part of the log schema.
- Audit logs & retention: We export provisioning events as JSON or CSV; events include timestamp, actor (email/service), token/client_id, action type, object id, pre/post diff (if configured), and HTTP request id. Default retention is 90 days for detailed logs, 2 years for aggregated/event-level summaries. Longer retention is available as an add-on.

I'll drop a small mapping example in the thread (scim_mapping_examples.json) and propose a short agenda for the workshop:
1) Walk SCIM mapping examples (30m)
2) Reconciliation semantics and tombstones (20m)
3) RBAC delegation patterns and demo (25m)
4) Q&A and next steps (15m)

If that looks good I can have the integration engineer run a dry test on a 5k test dataset next week.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Integration Engineer
Redwood Inference
